sources.name: Peace Services
openingWords: All Jewish services are peace services. At the center of everything is
There are so many things that we cannot control that threaten the

blocks.en: All Jewish services are peace services. At the center of everything is Shalom—wholeness— One of the many names for God.

There are so many things that we cannot control that threaten the lives of our children. For these we pray to God. But there are so many things that we can control: battering, neglect, and abuse hunger, poverty a toxic planet and global warming, racism and intolerance, and the ultimate threat – nuclear war. To end these, we turn to each other.

sources.name: Keva Kavannah Note
openingWords: For generations we have struggled between keva and kavannah in our liturgy.

blocks.en: For generations we have struggled between keva and kavannah in our liturgy. Keva is the fixed order of the service that allows us to find familiarity from service to service and commonality with Jews praying in all corners of the world. Kavannah is the creative thought, word or movement that adds meaning to the keva. The keva is here, along with some kavannot that reflect the spiritual journey of CRC members. Other kavannot are for us to add.

sources.name: Every Word a World
openingWords: Every single word is a whole world.

blocks.en: Every single word is a whole world.
~ Rabbi Nachman of Bratslav

sources.name: Will
openingWords: Three generations back my family had only to light a candle and

blocks.en: Three generations back my family had only to light a candle and the world parted. Today, Friday afternoon, I disconnect clocks and phones. When night fills my house with passages, I begin saving my life.
~ Marcia Falk

sources.name: House of Prayer
openingWords: And they shall come to my holy mountain And rejoice in my

blocks.en: And they shall come to my holy mountain And rejoice in my house of prayer My house shall be A house of prayer for all peoples.
~ Isaiah 56:7 Melody: Rabbi Aryeh Hirschfield

sources.name: Candle Lighting Song
openingWords: Hear our prayers we sing to you Be gracious to the ones

blocks.en: Hear our prayers we sing to you Be gracious to the ones we love And bless them with goodness and mercy and peace Oh, hear our prayers to you Let us light these lights And see our way to you And let us say: Amen
~ Debbie Friedman

sources.name: Candles Kavannah
openingWords: Why do we wave our hands in circular motions? There are many

blocks.en: Why do we wave our hands in circular motions? There are many explanations. We lift our hands over the flames six times to bring all six days into Shabbat. We draw the light into ourselves and spread the light to those in need. Why do we close our eyes? To complete the blessing before enjoying the light and to remember to use the light to look in as well as out.

sources.name: Angels Kavannah
openingWords: According to the Talmud (Shabbat 119), two angels accompany each of us

blocks.en: According to the Talmud (Shabbat 119), two angels accompany each of us on our way home from the synagogue on Erev Shabbat. One angel is good and the other is evil. Upon arriving home, if we have done anything to prepare for the Sabbath, the good angel brings blessings. If not, the evil one works mischief. Shalom Aleichem, based upon this legend, is Kabbalistic in origin.

sources.name: Shabbat Presence L’chah Dodi Kavannah
openingWords: The text of L'chah Dodi was written by Rabbi Shlomo Halevi of

blocks.en: The text of L'chah Dodi was written by Rabbi Shlomo Halevi of S'fat. Inspired by Kabbalistic imagery of union and integration, it reminds us of the 16th century custom of going out into the fields dressed in white to receive the presence of Shabbat, which some imagine as the Sabbath Bride, and invites us to call to that which will make us whole. We rise for the last verse and face the opening into our sanctuary hoping to glimpse the presence of the shalom of Shabbat.

sources.name: As We Bless
openingWords: As we bless the source of life, so we are blessed. And

blocks.en: As we bless the source of life, so we are blessed. And our blessings give us strength, and make our visions clear. And our blessings give us peace and the courage to dare. As we bless the source of life, so we are blessed.
~ Faith Rogow

sources.name: Barchu Kavannah Zohar
openingWords: Just as they in heaven above unite into Oneness, so the Sabbath
When the Sabbath arrives, she is placed by herself, separated from the
This prayer service is to bless her with joy and the light

blocks.en: Just as they in heaven above unite into Oneness, so the Sabbath on earth below joins the mystery of Oneness … as it is here, so it is there. This is the secret of Shabbat: Shabbat is attached to the secret of Oneness, Oneness that descends through the Shabbat evening prayer.

When the Sabbath arrives, she is placed by herself, separated from the Other Side. All manner of strife is kept from her; she remains in union with the holy light. All tyranny and affliction flee from her and vanish. There is no higher realm in the entire universe. Her face is illuminated with a higher light. On earth she is crowned by holy people who are endowed with new souls.

This prayer service is to bless her with joy and the light of rapture. In the Bar'chu we bless "et" which is Shechinah, the bride, the inner notion, and then we bless Hashem, the Holy One, the outer notion. The secret is: our prayer inspires the union. This is the deep secret of Shabbat, called "raza deShabbat." This poem initiates the Raza, the Secret, of Shabbat that bestirs in us the ancient memory of shalom; of wholeness that preceded separation and alienation.
~ from the Zohar

sources.name: Barchu Kavannah Talmud
openingWords: Jewish tradition emphasizes praying with a community. The Talmud says, "One who
As the first word, Bar'chu, is spoken, we bow slightly to gently

blocks.en: Jewish tradition emphasizes praying with a community. The Talmud says, "One who prays with the congregation will have their prayer answered."

As the first word, Bar'chu, is spoken, we bow slightly to gently call each other to prayer and to acknowledge each other's presence. The leader calls us to prayer. We respond that we are ready to pray

sources.name: Maariv Aravim Kavannah
openingWords: The blessings offered before and after the Sh'ma are deliberate. First, we
A great musician was once asked, "How do you play the notes

blocks.en: The blessings offered before and after the Sh'ma are deliberate. First, we marvel at the wisdom of creation, Ma-ariv Aravim. Then we are loved unconditionally, Ahavat Olam. With the Sh'ma we proclaim the unity of all things emanating from the Source. We cover our eyes with our hand sensing that we are part of a greater whole. Knowing that we are loved, we are able and willing to love back and are told how to do so in the V'ahavta. But the final section of the V'ahavta, V'haya Im Shemoa, contains a collective warning that is most appropriate for our time. If we do not care for all life, we will surely perish. The Sh'ma concludes with two blessings of redemption, Mi Chamochah and Hashkiveinu. The world, we remind ourselves, moves from the way things are to the way they ought to be. The repair of the heart and repair of the world are possible.

A great musician was once asked, "How do you play the notes so perfectly?" The artist replied, "The notes can be played by anyone; it is the pause between the notes that give them their beauty and meaning." On this Shabbat, we pause.

sources.name: Maariv Aravim Evening Chant
openingWords: Evening, the evenings, even-ing the frayed edges of our lives, ma-ariv aravim,

blocks.en: Evening, the evenings, even-ing the frayed edges of our lives, ma-ariv aravim, Amen.
~ Rabbi Geela Rayzel Raphael

sources.name: The Shma Kavannah
openingWords: The Sh'ma—Deuteronomy 6:4—is a call from God to Israel, from each one

blocks.en: The Sh'ma—Deuteronomy 6:4—is a call from God to Israel, from each one of us to the other. The second verse is a whispered response of awe. The source of this verse is rabbinic and is said aloud only on Yom Kippur, recalling the custom of the High Priest in the ancient Temple.

openingWords: The word emet literally means truth. In rabbinic practice, it is added

blocks.en: The word emet literally means truth. In rabbinic practice, it is added directly to the end of the Sh'ma as an immediate affirmation of its truth for us.

sources.name: Vahavta Thou Shalt Love
openingWords: And thou shalt love Adonai thy God with all of thy heart
And all these words which I command you on this day shall
And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children. And thou shalt
And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thy hand and
And thou shalt write them on the doorposts of thy house and

blocks.en: And thou shalt love Adonai thy God with all of thy heart with all thy soul and with all of thy might.
And all these words which I command you on this day shall be in thy heart.
And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children. And thou shalt speak of them when thou sittest in thy house, when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down and when thou risest up.
And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thy hand and they shall be for frontlets between thine eyes.
And thou shalt write them on the doorposts of thy house and upon thy gates that ye may remember and do all of my commandments and be holy unto your God

sources.name: Mi Chamochah Kavannah
openingWords: Tradition calls us to remember Yetziat Mitzrayim – our going out from

blocks.en: Tradition calls us to remember Yetziat Mitzrayim – our going out from Egypt – in every service. We remember that we were slaves and affirm that until all people are free, not one of us is completely free. Though we mourn for the suffering of the Egyptians and know that the journey ahead is long and difficult, we join together in celebration of this precious moment of freedom. The wisdom of celebrating that moment has carried us through times of deep despair when a glimmer of hope came from remembering the miracle at the shores of the sea when Miriam the prophetess took her timbrel in her hand and together with Moses led the people in song and dance.

sources.name: Vshamru Kavannah
openingWords: V'shamru is taken from Exodus 31:16-17. Shabbat is created to give us

blocks.en: V'shamru is taken from Exodus 31:16-17. Shabbat is created to give us rest and to restore the soul. Vayinafash is from the Hebrew word nefesh (soul). Shabbat is the promise that there will be a time of peace when all souls will be renewed. As we guard Shabbat, so Shabbat guards us and renews our souls.

sources.name: Chatzi Kaddish Kavannah
openingWords: Kaddish comes from the Hebrew word for holiness. There are five variations

blocks.en: Kaddish comes from the Hebrew word for holiness. There are five variations of the Kaddish prayer. This Kaddish is called the Hatzi Kaddish or half Kaddish because it omits one verse from the basic version. It is also called the Reader's Kaddish because it is used to separate the different parts of the service and offer a holy transition. Because our connection with the Kaddish is with mourning, we include the Reader's Kaddish to tell mourners they are welcome here, to praise the Source of Life and to separate the call to prayer from the T'filah. May our praying together move us from the way things are to the way they might be.

sources.name: T’filah Kavannah
openingWords: The central part of the prayer service is the T'filah, the Hebrew

blocks.en: The central part of the prayer service is the T'filah, the Hebrew word for prayer. It is also called Amidah (Standing) and Sh'moneh Esreh (Eighteen) because in the weekday service it originally contained 18 (today 19) blessings and was said standing. Once this was the time for the spontaneous prayers of the congregation. The more popular prayers were preserved. These became keva. The kavannot, our own personal blessings and hopes, are for us to add.

sources.name: Silent Amidah Note
openingWords: On Friday night, it is our custom to say the T'filah in
The Amidah that is said on weekdays is also known as Sh'moneh
Our silent meditation allows us time to reflect on these themes and
1. Avot v'imahot Holding on to the coat tails of our ancestors

blocks.en: On Friday night, it is our custom to say the T'filah in silence with the traditional prayers (found on pages 27 to 32) or with personal meditation. When you are done, please be seated.

The Amidah that is said on weekdays is also known as Sh'moneh Esreh, which means 18, because it once included 18 prayers. Now the daily Amidah has 19 prayers. We are told the middle thirteen prayers of the daily Amidah were omitted from the Shabbat service because the rabbis thought these prayers were reminders of problems and needs and therefore did not fit with the intended mood of joy on Shabbat. They were replaced by the K'dushat HaYom. Each of these blessings has its own theme.
Our silent meditation allows us time to reflect on these themes and add our own. The prayers of the daily Amidah are:

1. Avot v'imahot Holding on to the coat tails of our ancestors 2. G'vurot Seeking strength of body and spirit 3. K'dushah Filling the spaces between us with holiness 4. Binah Understanding (Da-at: Knowledge) (Chochmah: Wisdom) 5. T'shuvah Repentance – turning – the possibility of transformation 6. Slichah Forgiveness 7. G'ulah Redemption 8. R'fuah Healing 9. Birkat Hashanim A year of blessing 10. Kibbutz Galuyot Return from exile 11. Din Justice 12. Birkat Haminim Humbling the arrogant 13. Tzaddikim Righteous role models 14. Binyan Yerushalayim The rebuilding of Jerusalem 15. Malkut Beit David Hope for a Messianic Age – a time of peace for all creation 16. Sh'ma Koleinu Hear our voice and our prayer 17. Avodah Receive our offerings 18. Hoda-ah Gratitude 19. Birkat Shalom Blessing of peace

sources.name: Kedushat Hayom Tail
openingWords: You have made the seventh day holy in your name marking the
Our God and God of ages past may our rest on this

blocks.en: You have made the seventh day holy in your name marking the end of the creation of heaven and earth. You have blessed it above other days, and made it holy above other festivals, as it is written in your Torah: "Heaven and earth were finished, with all their array. On the seventh day God finished the work and rested. And God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, for on this day God rested from the work of creation."

Our God and God of ages past may our rest on this day be pleasing in your sight. Sanctify us with your mitzvot and let your Torah be our way of life. Satisfy us with your goodness, gladden us with your salvation, and purify our hearts to serve you in truth. In your gracious love, our God, let Shabbat remain our heritage, that all Israel, hallowing your name, may find rest and peace. Blessed is God, for the holiness of Shabbat.

sources.name: Prayer for State of Israel
openingWords: We pray for the land of Israel and its people. May its

blocks.en: We pray for the land of Israel and its people. May its borders know peace and its inhabitants, tranquility. And may the bonds of faith and fate which unite the Jews of all lands be a source of strength to Israel and to us all. God of all lands and ages, answer our constant prayer with a Zion once more aglow with light for us and for all the world, and let us say: Amen.

sources.name: Aleinu Kavannah
openingWords: This prayer reminds us that we are no longer victims. We must

blocks.en: This prayer reminds us that we are no longer victims. We must be on guard to avoid becoming like those nations who oppress. We bow at the word korim in humility and gratitude as we learn from the lessons of our own history and commit ourselves to tikkun olam – the restoration of wholeness to our broken world.

sources.name: Bayom Hahu
openingWords: And then all that has divided us will merge And then compassion

blocks.en: And then all that has divided us will merge And then compassion will be wedded to power And then softness will come to a world that is harsh and unkind And then both men and women will be gentle And then both women and men will be strong And then no person will be subject to another's will And then all will be rich and free and varied And then the greed of some will give way to the needs of many And then all will share equally in the Earth's abundance And then all will care for the sick and the weak and the old And then all will nourish the young And then all will cherish life's creatures And then all will live in harmony with each other and the Earth And then everywhere will be called Eden once again.
~Judy Chicago

sources.name: Mourners Kaddish Kavannah
openingWords: As all our prayers, the Mourner's Kaddish connects us with the Source

blocks.en: As all our prayers, the Mourner's Kaddish connects us with the Source of Life. We rise together and say these same words that our people have said for their loved ones and for all those who have no one to say Kaddish for them to continue the blessings of their lives: for those caught in the crossfire of violence; the victims of the Holocaust; those who have died because of hunger and homelessness; those who have died from AIDS, cancer and other diseases we cannot yet cure.

blocks.en: It is customary to bless children, old and young, on Shabbat, either in the synagogue or at home for protection, for healing, and as an expression of love.

sources.name: How to Use
openingWords: There is a Chassidic story about prayer in the forest. Once we
The traditional service has five parts. The first part of the service

blocks.en: There is a Chassidic story about prayer in the forest. Once we gathered in a sacred place in the forest and lit fires and danced and sang songs and told the story of our people to our children. The next generation forgot their way to the sacred place where they lit fires but they continued to dance and to sing the songs and tell the story of our people to our children. The next generation forgot the dance but continued to sing and to tell the story. The next generation forgot the songs but continued to tell the story of our people to our children. The story ends with the words, "and this was enough.” For us it is not enough. Our task is to reclaim the dance, sing the songs, tell the story and light the fires to create our sacred place. Let sparks of wisdom and goodness light the darkness each and every time we gather as community in prayer together. For generations we have struggled between keva and kavannah in our liturgy. Keva is the fixed order of the service that allows us to find familiarity from service to service and commonality with Jews praying in all corners of the world. Kavannah is the creative thought, word or movement that adds meaning to the keva prayers. The keva is here, along with some kavannot that reflect the spiritual journey of CRC members. Other kavannot are for us to add.

The traditional service has five parts. The first part of the service that we call Awakening opens our hearts and helps us prepare for prayer. The Sh’ma and Her Blessings includes our call to communal prayer and our lessons on walking in the world, celebrating the connectedness of creation. The T’filah gives us the opportunity to express our most personal prayers, deepening our connection to the wisdom of our tradition and reminding us to reach toward a time of peace and redemption for all creation. The Torah Service leads us in joyful learning, guided by the Torah and Haftarah portions. The Concluding Prayers prepare us to take the peace we have found into the many holy opportunities for service and tikkun in the week to come, inspiring us to be more courageous, caring, and kind.

sources.name: Chatzi Kaddish Kavannah
openingWords: Kaddish comes from the Hebrew word for holiness. There are five variations

blocks.en: Kaddish comes from the Hebrew word for holiness. There are five variations of the Kaddish prayer. This Kaddish is called the Hatzi Kaddish or half Kaddish because it omits one verse from the basic version. It is also called the Reader's Kaddish because it is used to separate the different parts of the service and offer a holy transition. Because our connection with the Kaddish is with mourning, we include the Reader's Kaddish to tell mourners they are welcome here, to praise the Source of Life and to separate the preparation for prayer from our call to prayer. May our praying together move us from the way things are to the way they might be.

blocks.en: Jewish tradition emphasizes praying with a community. The Talmud says, "One who prays with the congregation will have their prayer answered."

As the first word, Bar'chu, is spoken, we bow slightly to gently call each other to prayer and to acknowledge each other's presence. The leader calls us to prayer. We respond that we are ready to pray.

sources.name: Yotzer Or Interpretation
openingWords: In some special way every person completes the universe. If I do

blocks.en: In some special way every person completes the universe. If I do not play my part, I injure the pattern of all existence. The same stream of life that runs through my veins night and day Runs through the world and dances in rhythmic measures. It is the same life that shoots in joy through the dust of the earth In numberless blades of grass And breaks into tumultuous waves of leaves and flowers. It is the same life that is rocked In the ocean cradle of birth and death, In ebb and flow. I feel my limbs are made glorious By the touch of this world of life. And my pride is from the life throb Of ages dancing in my blood this moment.
~ R. Tagore

sources.name: Unending Love
openingWords: We are loved by an unending love. We are embraced by arms

blocks.en: We are loved by an unending love. We are embraced by arms that find us even when we are hidden from ourselves. We are touched by fingers that soothe us even when we are too proud for soothing. We are counseled by voices that guide us even when we are too embittered to hear. We are loved by an unending love. We are supported by hands that uplift us even in the midst of a fall. We are urged on by eyes that meet us even when we are too weak for meeting. We are loved by an unending love. Embraced, touched, soothed, and counseled. Ours are the arms, the fingers, the voices; Ours are the hands, the eyes, the smiles; We are loved by an unending love. Blessed are you, God, who loves your people Israel (and all creation).
~ Rabbi Rami M. Shapiro

sources.name: Kriyat Sh’ma Teaching
openingWords: Why are the ע and the ד written larger?
The first line of the Sh'ma is so important that the words
Why do we cover our eyes when we say the Sh'ma?
Knowing that we are not alone, that we are safe and secure

blocks.en: Why are the ע and the ד written larger?

The first line of the Sh'ma is so important that the words שמע and אחד are written in a special way. The ע in שמע and the ד in אחד are written larger than the other letters so people will not misread them. If the ע were mistaken for an א, the word would mean "perhaps" instead of "hear". If the ד were read as a ר, the meaning would change from "one" to "another". Clearly, the phrase, "Perhaps, Israel, Adonai is our God, Adonai is other" is very different from "Hear Israel, Adonai is our God, Adonai is One". Furthermore, ע and ד together make the word עד which means "witness" or the word עד which means "forever". So, when we say the Sh'ma, we become witnesses to God's unity and continual existence. The big letter ד teaches us that God is everywhere. The letter ד is also the number four. When we see a big ד we remember that God can be found at all corners of the earth.
Why do we cover our eyes when we say the Sh'ma?
Knowing that we are not alone, that we are safe and secure in our shelter of peace, we cover our eyes to find the sacred spaces and hidden sparks within.
~ Rambam, Mishneh Torah

sources.name: Kriyat Sh’ma Kavannah
openingWords: The Sh'ma—Deuteronomy 6:4—is a call from God to Israel, from each one

blocks.en: The Sh'ma—Deuteronomy 6:4—is a call from God to Israel, from each one of us to the other. The second verse is a response, whispered in humble acceptance of the connectedness of all creation. The source of this verse is rabbinic and is said aloud only on Yom Kippur, recalling the custom of the High Priest in the ancient Temple.

blocks.en: Traditionally, this is the second paragraph of the Sh'ma which today reminds us of the ecological and environmental consequences of our collective actions.

And if you listen intently to My mitzvot which I am making your mitzvot this very day showing your love for Yah your God and giving service with every inclination of your knowing heart and all the strength with which you live Then shall I give your land rain in its proper time autumn rain and spring rain that you may harvest your grain your wine and your oil. sources.name: Mi Chamocha Kavannah
openingWords: Tradition calls us to remember Yetziat Mitzrayim – our going out from

blocks.en: Tradition calls us to remember Yetziat Mitzrayim – our going out from Egypt – in every service. We remember that we were slaves and affirm that until all people are free, not one of us is completely free. Though we mourn for the suffering of the Egyptians and know that the journey ahead is long and difficult, we join together in celebration of this precious moment of freedom. The wisdom of celebrating that moment has carried us through times of deep despair when a glimmer of hope came from remembering the miracle at the shores of the sea when Miriam the prophetess took her timbrel in her hand and together with Moses led the people in song and dance.

sources.name: T’filah Kavannah
openingWords: The central part of the prayer service is the T’filah, the Hebrew

blocks.en: The central part of the prayer service is the T’filah, the Hebrew word for prayer. It is also called Amidah (Standing) and Sh’moneh Esreh (Eighteen) because in the weekday service it originally contained 18 (today 19) blessings and was said standing. The Shabbat and holiday Amidah, called T’filat Sheva (seven) is composed of the first three and the last three prayers of the daily Amidah plus a special prayer for holidays and Shabbat (Kedushat Hayom). The blessings praise, petition and thank God. Once this was the time for the spontaneous prayers of the congregation. The more popular prayers were preserved. These became keva. The kavannot, our own personal blessings and hopes, are for us to add.

openingWords: The K’dushah is composed of verses from the Prophets and the Psalms.

blocks.en: The K’dushah is composed of verses from the Prophets and the Psalms. The form of the prayer is call and response. The custom to rise up on our tip-toes while reciting the first response recalls Isaiah’s vision of angels witnessing the fullness of God’s presence calling, “Holy, Holy, Holy.” Reaching towards the heavens, we connect the heavens and the earth, filling the spaces between us with holiness.

blocks.en: V'shamru is taken from Exodus 31:16-17. Shabbat is created to give us rest and to restore the soul. Vayinafash is from the Hebrew word nefesh (soul). Shabbat is the promise that there will be a time of peace when all souls will be renewed. As we guard Shabbat, so Shabbat guards us and renews our souls.

sources.name: The Nineteen Blessings
openingWords: The Amidah that is said on weekdays is also known as Sh'moneh
Our silent meditation allows us time to reflect on these themes and
The prayers of the daily Amidah are:
1. Avot v'imahot — Holding on to the coattails of our ancestors

blocks.en: The Amidah that is said on weekdays is also known as Sh'moneh Esreh, which means 18, because it once included 18 prayers. Now the daily Amidah has 19 prayers. We are told the middle thirteen prayers of the daily Amidah were omitted from the Shabbat service because the rabbis thought these prayers were reminders of problems and needs and therefore did not fit with the intended mood of joy on Shabbat. They were replaced by the K'dushat HaYom. Each of these blessings has its own theme.
Our silent meditation allows us time to reflect on these themes and add our own.
The prayers of the daily Amidah are:

1. Avot v'imahot — Holding on to the coattails of our ancestors 2. G'vurot — Seeking strength of body and spirit 3. K'dushah — Filling the spaces between us with holiness 4. Binah — Understanding (Da-at: Knowledge) (Chochmah: Wisdom) 5. T'shuvah — Repentance – turning – the possibility of transformation 6. Slichah — Forgiveness 7. G'ulah — Redemption 8. R'fuah — Healing 9. Birkat Hashanim — A year of blessing 10. Kibbutz Galuyot — Return from exile 11. Din — Justice 12. Birkat Haminim — Humbling the arrogant 13. Tzaddikim — Righteous role models 14. Binyan Yerushalayim — The rebuilding of Jerusalem 15. Malkut Beit David — Hope for a Messianic Age – a time of peace for all creation 16. Sh'ma Koleinu — Hear our voice and our prayer 17. Avodah — Receive our offerings 18. Hoda-ah — Gratitude 19. Birkat Shalom — Blessing of peace

sources.name: Prayer for Israel
openingWords: We pray for the land of Israel and its people. May its

blocks.en: We pray for the land of Israel and its people. May its borders know peace and its inhabitants, tranquility. And may the bonds of faith and fate which unite the Jews of all lands be a source of strength to Israel and to us all. God of all lands and ages, answer our constant prayer with a Zion once more aglow with light for us and for all the world and let us say: Amen.

openingWords: Shechinah, we know your presence is here with us. You are the

We ask your blessing on all those engaged in tikkun olam, the

blocks.en: Shechinah, we know your presence is here with us. You are the peace and joy of our days. But we also know that you dwell in the depths of suffering and sorrow.

We pray now for the hungry, for the homeless, for the victims of war and catastrophe, for the sick and the dying, for those oppressed by racism. And we pray for our fragile earth, for all her inhabitants, and for life itself.

We ask your blessing on all those engaged in tikkun olam, the healing and transforming of our planet. Open our hearts and stir us to struggle on behalf of your creations. May each of us, all of us, become your limbs and hands, bringing healing and compassion, social justice, love, and peace to your world.

blocks.en: We are dreamers, people with a vision. We are people who have not allowed our dream of a more perfect time to be tainted or trampled by those who have threatened to take our dream away from us.

That more perfect time we speak of is a picture in our own highest, inextinguishable imaginings! Can we imagine a completed time, a time of peace, of completedness yes! We do imagine it. That is always the point...
On That Day, of our completed time, we recognize the relatedness of all things, all things are connected, its Name is One, and that One is God.
On That Day is our awakening. It is not the end of history, it's the very beginning.
On That Day, we begin the upward course, to a more perfect time...never arriving always becoming, always becoming.
~ Rabbi James Stone Goodman

blocks.en: And then all that has divided us will merge And then compassion will be wedded to power And then softness will come to a world that is harsh and unkind And then both men and women will be gentle And then both women and men will be strong And then no person will be subject to another's will And then all will be rich and free and varied And then the greed of some will give way to the needs of many And then all will share equally in the Earth's abundance And then all will care for the sick and the weak and the old And then all will nourish the young And then all will cherish life's creatures And then all will live in harmony with each other and the Earth And then everywhere will be called Eden once again.

sources.name: Mourner’s Kaddish Kavannah
openingWords: As all our prayers, the Mourner's Kaddish connects us with the Source

blocks.en: As all our prayers, the Mourner's Kaddish connects us with the Source of Life. We rise together and say these same words that our people have said for their loved ones and for all those who have no one to say Kaddish for them to continue the blessings of their lives: for those caught in the crossfire of violence; the victims of the Holocaust; those who have died because of hunger and homelessness; those who have died from AIDS, cancer and other diseases we cannot yet cure.

sources.name: Welcome
openingWords: We are grateful you are with us to celebrate as one of

blocks.en: Central Reform Congregation

We are grateful you are with us to celebrate as one of our precious young people becomes a Beit Mitzvah. In Hebrew “beit” means “house.” At CRC, we use the general term Beit Mitzvah to “house” the many ways our young people and their families choose to name this journey: Bar Mitzvah, Bat Mitzvah, B-Mitzvah, B’not Mitzvah, or B’nei Mitzvah. This coming-of-age ceremony is how Jewish tradition marks the transition as our students move from childhood to their teen years and approach young adulthood. This means they are becoming more mature, more independent, and more responsible for their actions. It is at this precise point of Beit Mitzvah that the students demonstrate that they have the tools to bring their Judaism with them as adults. We believe these skills will help them lead meaningful, ethical, and purposeful lives. Our young people have worked hard, often for many years, to be able to lead you today in prayer and in Torah. Throughout our Siddur, our prayer book, you will find Hebrew, transliteration, service explanations, direct translations, and poetic interpretations. At various moments throughout the service, our young person will share their kavannah/kavannot. These are quotations or reflections they have chosen or created that relate to the themes of the prayers. Our services are musical and participatory, and we invite you to join us in prayer and song as you are comfortable. We are so proud of each and every student as they become Beit Mitzvah, and we are grateful for this sacred community that embraces our young people on their life journeys.

sources.name: An Explanation of Our Siddur Prayer Book
openingWords: The traditional Shabbat service has five parts. The first part of the

blocks.en: The traditional Shabbat service has five parts. The first part of the service, which we call Awakening, opens our hearts and helps us prepare for prayer; this is our warm-up. The Sh’ma and Its Blessings includes our call to communal prayer and our lessons on walking in the world; celebrating the connectedness of creation. The Prayers gives us the opportunity to pray both as a community and an individual, giving us a chance to express our most personal prayers. The Torah Service leads us in joyful learning, guided by the Torah and Haftarah portions. This is the most important part of our service, and our Beit Mitzvah students spend many years preparing for this section. The Concluding Prayers prepare us to take the peace we have found into the many holy opportunities for service and tikkun (repair) in the week to come, inspiring us to be more courageous, caring, and kind.

sources.name: May the Door
openingWords: May the door of this synagogue be wide enough to receive all
~ Words from Gates of Repentance and music by Bonia Shur

blocks.en: May the door of this synagogue be wide enough to receive all who hunger for love, all who are lonely for fellowship. May it welcome all who have cares to unburden, thanks to express, hopes to nurture. May the door of this synagogue be narrow enough to shut out pettiness and pride, envy, and enmity. May this threshold be no stumbling block to young or straying feet. May it be too high to admit complacency, selfishness and harshness. May this synagogue be for all who enter the doorway to a richer and more meaningful life. Amen.
~ Words from Gates of Repentance and music by Bonia Shur

blocks.en: God, in awe and humility we have come together to pray.
Our prayers are filled with You. Yet speaking Your Name, quite frankly, we get stuck.
In Your Name books and people have been burnt.
In Your Name souls have been stolen.
In Your Name ideas have been suppressed, and
In Your Name passions have been aroused and disappointed.

But we are Israel. Our name in Hebrew means, "the people who struggle with God". And struggle with You we do. Like Abraham who fought for the righteous in Sodom and Gemorah. Like Sarah who laughed at your timing. We struggle with You and each one of us understands You differently.
For some You are like a loving parent.
For some You are the illusive spark of life itself.
Some blame You for all the evil in the world.
You are what makes many reach for the good even when there is so much pain.
Others have seen You at the side of the suffering, suffering with them.

Though we often speak of You in one voice with these prayers that we are about to utter, to each of us here You are something different. We will try not to limit our imaginings of You. When we speak of You smiling upon us, we know that for many of us the smiles we imagine are on the faces of the people we love. As we learn to liberate You, may we learn to grant freedom to all humankind. As You smile upon us, Please God, teach us to smile upon each other.
~ Susan

sources.name: Yahrzeit Candles
openingWords: Traditionally one would light a yahrzeit candle for parents in preparation for
Let this light help us to praise them and if need be,
Tonight we also light this light for quiet heroes martyrs soldiers victims
For the good we will not know because they died too young,
We light this light for them, may their memories be a blessing.

blocks.en: Traditionally one would light a yahrzeit candle for parents in preparation for Yom Kippur. Our candle is lit for parents, grandparents, spouses, children, siblings; for all those whose lives graced ours.
Let this light help us to praise them and if need be, let this light show us the way to forgive them.

Tonight we also light this light for quiet heroes martyrs soldiers victims of cancer of AIDS of Alzheimer's of other diseases with no known cure those who perished in the holocaust of our people victims of violence
For the good we will not know because they died too young, we light this light to remind us that their dreams and their visions of a better world are now ours to bring to reality.
We light this light for them, may their memories be a blessing.

sources.name: Memorial Reading 1
openingWords: If some messenger were to come to us with the offer that
We shall not fear the summons of death; we shall remember those
"Alas for those who cannot sing, but die with all their music
Help us, God, to fulfill the promise that is in each of

blocks.en: If some messenger were to come to us with the offer that death should be overthrown, but with the one inseparable condition that birth should also cease; if the existing generation were given the chance to live for ever, but on the clear understanding that never again would there be a child, or a youth, or first love, never again new persons with new hopes, new ideas, new achievements; ourselves for always and never any others— could the answer be in doubt?
We shall not fear the summons of death; we shall remember those who have gone before us, and those who come after us.

"Alas for those who cannot sing, but die with all their music in them." Let us treasure the time we have, and resolve to use it well, counting each moment precious—a chance to apprehend some truth, to experience some beauty, to conquer some evil, to relieve some suffering, to love and be loved, to achieve something of lasting worth.

Help us, God, to fulfill the promise that is in each of us, and so to conduct ourselves that, generations hence, it will be true to say of us: The world is better because, for a brief space, they lived in it.

sources.name: Memorial Reading 2
openingWords: At this hour of memorial we recall with grief all Your children
They lie in nameless graves, in far-off forests and lonely fields. And
We pray to You, O Source of mercy, that Your Torah, to
We remember with sorrow those whom death has taken from our midst
Taking these dear ones into our hearts with all our beloved, we

blocks.en: At this hour of memorial we recall with grief all Your children who have perished through the cruelty of the oppressor, victims of demonic hate: the aged and young, the learned and unlettered—all driven in multitudes along the road of pain and pitiless death. Their very presence on earth was begrudged them, for they brought Your covenant of mercy and justice to the recollection of Your enemies; they perished because they were a symbol of Your eternal law; their death has brought darkness to the human soul.

They lie in nameless graves, in far-off forests and lonely fields. And the substance of many was scattered by the winds to the earth's four corners. Yet they shall not be forgotten. We take them into our hearts and give them a place beside the cherished memories of our own loved ones. They are now ours.

We pray to You, O Source of mercy, that Your Torah, to which these Your children bore witness in life and in death, may come to glow with a renewed light in the human soul; that, remembering them, we may sanctify Your name in all the world. Thus will their memory become an enduring blessing to all Your children.
We remember with sorrow those whom death has taken from our midst during the past year. Let us rise and remember….
Taking these dear ones into our hearts with all our beloved, we recall them now with reverence.

sources.name: We Remember Them
openingWords: In the rising of the sun and in its going down, we

blocks.en: In the rising of the sun and in its going down, we remember them. In the blowing of the wind and in the chill of winter, we remember them. In the opening buds and in the rebirth of spring, we remember them. In the blueness of the sky and in the warmth of summer, we remember them. In the rustling of leaves and in the beauty of autumn, we remember them. In the beginning of the year and when it ends, we remember them. When we are weary and in need of strength, we remember them. When we are lost and sick at heart, we remember them. When we have joys we yearn to share, we remember them. So long as we live, they too shall live, for they are now a part of us, as we remember them.

sources.name: Tshuvah Reading
openingWords: Now is the time for turning. The leaves are beginning to turn
We are called to respond with "hineini", the kind of radical presence

blocks.en: Now is the time for turning. The leaves are beginning to turn from green to red and orange. The birds are beginning to turn and are heading once more toward the South. The animals are beginning to turn to storing their food for the winter. For leaves, birds, and animals turning comes instinctively. But for us turning does not come so easily. It takes an act of will for us to make a turn. It means breaking with old habits. It means admitting that we have been wrong; and this is never easy. It means losing face; it means starting all over again; and this is always painful. It means saying: I am sorry. It means recognizing that we have the ability to change. These things are terribly hard to do. But unless we turn, we will be trapped forever in yester- day's ways. God, help us to turn—from callousness to sensitivity, from hostility to love, from pettiness to purpose, from envy to contentment, from carelessness to discipline, from fear to faith. Turn us around, O God, and bring us back toward You. Revive our lives, as at the beginning. And turn us toward each other, God, for in isolation there is no life.
~ Gates of Repentance

We are called to respond with "hineini", the kind of radical presence and humility that bring us towards the promise of these Holy Days which is T'shuvah. T'shuvah means that change is possible: change in self, change in situation, change in relationships. Today is the day for repentance which will lead us to transformation. This is the path to shalom—wholeness and peace—for ourselves, our community, and our planet

openingWords: We pray for the land of Israel and its people. May its

blocks.en: We pray for the land of Israel and its people. May its borders know peace and its inhabitants, tranquility. And may the bonds of faith and fate which unite the Jews of all lands be a source of strength to Israel and to us all. God of all lands and ages, answer our constant prayer with a Zion once more aglow with light for us and for all the world, and let us say: Amen.

sources.name: Night Descends
openingWords: The night descends once more on the atoning sunlight of lives made
We have shared many words about ourselves this Atonement Day, confessing error,
Now the gates are closing in the heavens which have been the
The night descends and we, strengthened and renewed, arise.

blocks.en: The night descends once more on the atoning sunlight of lives made more profound and thoughtful by the words and hours we have spent together. What opened when the moon last rose as an Atonement Day has become At-one-ment Day, in which we have come closer to our people, have become more trusting of ourselves, and have lost some of the fears of the God before whom we have stood in awe. The night descends and we, strengthened and renewed, arise.

We have shared many words about ourselves this Atonement Day, confessing error, thoughtlessness, misdeed, and wrong. And yet the very act of confronting failings has enabled us to confront our virtue, and so what we must leave with each other this day is the conviction of our inner worth, the knowledge that no matter what we do we are the child of God, a valued and irreplaceable jewel in the crown that is God's universe.

Now the gates are closing in the heavens which have been the witness of our hearts on this afflicting, wearying, yet now exalting day. As the sun descends into the sea, we pray that it may take our misdeeds, thoughtlessness, and wrongs with it, that when the stars rise in the clear night sky there might rise with them the first and tender steps of a committed, thoughtful life, our soul awake to the brightness of possibilities that life can offer us, to enable us to shine among our cosmos as the full, bright Tishri moon that soon will glow above us in the Sukkot sky.
The night descends and we, strengthened and renewed, arise.

blocks.he: יְדִיד נֶפֶשׁ אָב הָרַחֲמָן, מְשׁוֹךְ עַבְדְּךָ אֶל רְצוֹנֶךָ. יָרוּץ עַבְדְּךָ כְּמוֹ אַיָּל, יִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה אֶל מוּל הֲדָרֶךָ. יֶעֱרַב לוֹ יְדִידוֹתֶיךָ, מִנֹּפֶת צוּף וְכָל טָעַם.
blocks.tr: Yedid nefesh, Av harachaman, m’shoch avd’cha el r’tzonecha. Yarutz avd’cha k’mo ayal, yishtachaveh el mul hadarecha. Ye’erav lo y’didotecha, minofet tzuf v’chol ta’am.

blocks.he: הָדוּר נָאֶה זִיו הָעוֹלָם, נַפְשִׁי חוֹלַת אַהֲבָתֶךָ. אָנָּא אֵל נָא רְפָא נָא לָהּ, בְּהַרְאוֹת לָהּ נֹעַם זִיוֶךָ. אָז תִּתְחַזֵּק וְתִתְרַפֵּא, וְהָיְתָה לָהּ שִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם.
blocks.tr: Hadur na’eh ziv ha’olam, nafshi cholat ahavatecha. Ana El na r’fa na lah, b’har’ot lah no’am zivecha. Az titchazek v’titrape, v’hayta lah simchat olam.

blocks.he: וָתִיק יֶהֱמוּ נָא רַחֲמֶיךָ, וְחוּסָה נָא עַל בֵּן אֲהוּבֶךָ. כִּי זֶה כַּמָּה נִכְסוֹף נִכְסַפְתִּי לִרְאוֹת מְהֵרָה בְּתִפְאֶרֶת עֻזֶּךָ. אֵלֶּה חָמְדָה לִבִּי, וְחוּסָה נָא וְאַל תִּתְעַלֵּם.
blocks.tr: Vatik, yehemu na rachamecha, v’chusa na al ben ahuvecha. Ki zeh kama nichsof nichsafti lir’ot m’hera b’tif’eret uzecha. Eleh chamda libi, v’chusa na v’al tit’alem.

blocks.he: הִגָּלֶה נָּא וּפְרוֹס חֲבִיבִי עָלַי אֶת סֻכַּת שְׁלוֹמֶךָ. תָּאִיר אֶרֶץ מִכְּבוֹדֶךָ, נָגִילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה בָּךְ. מַהֵר אֶהֹב כִּי בָא מוֹעֵד, וְחָנֵּנוּ כִּימֵי עוֹלָם.
blocks.tr: Higaleh na uf’ros, chavivi, alai et sukat sh’lomecha. Ta’ir eretz mik’vodecha, nagila v’nism’cha bach. Maher ehov ki va mo’ed, v’chonenu kimei olam.

אַל־תַּקְשׁוּ לְבַבְכֶם כִּמְרִיבָה, כְּיוֹם מַסָּה בַּמִּדְבָּר. אֲשֶׁר נִסּוּנִי אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם, בְּחָנוּנִי גַּם־רָאוּ פׇעֳלִי.
Al takshu l’vavchem kimriva, k’yom masa bamidbar. Asher nisuni avoteichem, b’chanuni gam

blocks.he: לְכוּ נְרַנְּנָה לַיְיָ נָרִיעָה לְצוּר יִשְׁעֵנוּ, נְקַדְּמָה פָנָיו בְּתוֹדָה בִּזְמִרוֹת נָרִיעַ לוֹ.
blocks.tr: L’chu n’ran’na la’Adonai, nari’a l’tzur yish’einu. N’kad’ma fanav b’toda, bizmirot nari’a lo.

blocks.he: כִּי אֵל גָּדוֹל יְיָ, וּמֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל עַל־כׇּל־אֱלֹהִים. אֲשֶׁר בְּיָדוֹ מֶחְקְרֵי־אָרֶץ וְתוֹעֲפֹת הָרִים לוֹ. אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ הַיָּם וְהוּא עָשָׂהוּ, וְיַבֶּשֶׁת יָדָיו יָצָרוּ.
blocks.tr: Ki El gadol Adonai, umelech gadol al kol elohim. Asher b’yado mechk’rei aretz, v’to’afot harim lo. Asher lo hayam v’hu asahu, v’yabeshet yadav yatzaru.

blocks.he: בֹּאוּ נִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה וְנִכְרָעָה, נִבְרְכָה לִפְנֵי־יְיָ עֹשֵׂנוּ. כִּי הוּא אֱלֹהֵינוּ, וַאֲנַחְנוּ עַם מַרְעִיתוֹ וְצֹאן יָדוֹ, הַיּוֹם אִם־בְּקֹלוֹ תִשְׁמָעוּ.
blocks.tr: Bo’u nishtachaveh v’nichra’a, nivr’cha lifnei Adonai osenu. Ki hu Eloheinu, va’anachnu am mar’ito v’tzon yado, hayom im b’kolo tishma’u.

blocks.he: אַל־תַּקְשׁוּ לְבַבְכֶם כִּמְרִיבָה, כְּיוֹם מַסָּה בַּמִּדְבָּר. אֲשֶׁר נִסּוּנִי אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם, בְּחָנוּנִי גַּם־רָאוּ פׇעֳלִי. אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה אָקוּט בְּדוֹר וָאֹמַר עַם תֹּעֵי לֵבָב הֵם, וְהֵם לֹא־יָדְעוּ דְרָכָי. אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי בְאַפִּי אִם־יְבֹאוּן אֶל־מְנוּחָתִי.
blocks.tr: Al takshu l’vavchem kimriva, k’yom masa bamidbar. Asher nisuni avoteichem, b’chanuni gam ra’u fo’oli. Arba’im shana akut b’dor, va’omar am to’ei levav hem, v’hem lo yad’u d’rachai. Asher nishba’ti v’api, im y’vo’un el m’nuchati.

sources.name: Psalm 96
aliases: Six psalms — one for each day of the week just ended — before we rise to greet Shabbat herself.
openingWords: שִׁירוּ לַיְיָ שִׁיר חָדָשׁ, שִׁירוּ לַיְיָ כׇּל־הָאָרֶץ. שִׁירוּ לַיְיָ בָּרְכוּ שְׁמוֹ, בַּשְּׂרוּ
Shiru la’Adonai shir chadash, shiru la’Adonai kol ha’aretz. Shiru la’Adonai barchu sh’mo,
כִּי גָדוֹל יְיָ וּמְהֻלָּל מְאֹד, נוֹרָא הוּא עַל־כׇּל־אֱלֹהִים. כִּי כׇּל־אֱלֹהֵי הָעַמִּים אֱלִילִים,
Ki gadol Adonai umhulal me’od, nora hu al kol elohim. Ki kol
הָבוּ לַיְיָ מִשְׁפְּחוֹת עַמִּים, הָבוּ לַיְיָ כָּבוֹד וָעֹז. הָבוּ לַיְיָ כְּבוֹד שְׁמוֹ,
Havu la’Adonai mishp’chot amim, havu la’Adonai kavod va’oz. Havu la’Adonai k’vod sh’mo,
אִמְרוּ בַגּוֹיִם יְיָ מָלָךְ, אַף־תִּכּוֹן תֵּבֵל בַּל־תִּמּוֹט, יָדִין עַמִּים בְּמֵישָׁרִים.
Imru vagoyim Adonai malach, af tikon tevel bal timot, yadin amim b’meisharim.

blocks.he: שִׁירוּ לַיְיָ שִׁיר חָדָשׁ, שִׁירוּ לַיְיָ כׇּל־הָאָרֶץ. שִׁירוּ לַיְיָ בָּרְכוּ שְׁמוֹ, בַּשְּׂרוּ מִיּוֹם־לְיוֹם יְשׁוּעָתוֹ. סַפְּרוּ בַגּוֹיִם כְּבוֹדוֹ, בְּכׇל־הָעַמִּים נִפְלְאוֹתָיו.
blocks.tr: Shiru la’Adonai shir chadash, shiru la’Adonai kol ha’aretz. Shiru la’Adonai barchu sh’mo, basru miyom l’yom yeshuato. Sap’ru vagoyim k’vodo, b’chol ha’amim nifl’otav.

blocks.he: כִּי גָדוֹל יְיָ וּמְהֻלָּל מְאֹד, נוֹרָא הוּא עַל־כׇּל־אֱלֹהִים. כִּי כׇּל־אֱלֹהֵי הָעַמִּים אֱלִילִים, וַיְיָ שָׁמַיִם עָשָׂה. הוֹד־וְהָדָר לְפָנָיו, עֹז וְתִפְאֶרֶת בְּמִקְדָּשׁוֹ.
blocks.tr: Ki gadol Adonai umhulal me’od, nora hu al kol elohim. Ki kol elohei ha’amim elilim, va’Adonai shamayim asa. Hod v’hadar l’fanav, oz v’tif’eret b’mikdasho.

blocks.he: הָבוּ לַיְיָ מִשְׁפְּחוֹת עַמִּים, הָבוּ לַיְיָ כָּבוֹד וָעֹז. הָבוּ לַיְיָ כְּבוֹד שְׁמוֹ, שְׂאוּ־מִנְחָה וּבֹאוּ לְחַצְרוֹתָיו. הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַיְיָ בְּהַדְרַת־קֹדֶשׁ, חִילוּ מִפָּנָיו כׇּל־הָאָרֶץ.
blocks.tr: Havu la’Adonai mishp’chot amim, havu la’Adonai kavod va’oz. Havu la’Adonai k’vod sh’mo, s’u mincha uvo’u l’chatzrotav. Hishtachavu la’Adonai b’hadrat kodesh, chilu mipanav kol ha’aretz.

blocks.he: אִמְרוּ בַגּוֹיִם יְיָ מָלָךְ, אַף־תִּכּוֹן תֵּבֵל בַּל־תִּמּוֹט, יָדִין עַמִּים בְּמֵישָׁרִים.
blocks.tr: Imru vagoyim Adonai malach, af tikon tevel bal timot, yadin amim b’meisharim.

blocks.he: יִשְׂמְחוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וְתָגֵל הָאָרֶץ, יִרְעַם הַיָּם וּמְלֹאוֹ. יַעֲלֹז שָׂדַי וְכׇל־אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ, אָז יְרַנְּנוּ כׇּל־עֲצֵי־יָעַר. לִפְנֵי יְיָ כִּי בָא, כִּי בָא לִשְׁפֹּט הָאָרֶץ, יִשְׁפֹּט־תֵּבֵל בְּצֶדֶק וְעַמִּים בֶּאֱמוּנָתוֹ.
blocks.tr: Yism’chu hashamayim v’tagel ha’aretz, yir’am hayam umlo’o. Ya’aloz sadai v’chol asher bo, az y’ran’nu kol atzei ya’ar. Lifnei Adonai ki va, ki va lishpot ha’aretz, yishpot tevel b’tzedek, v’amim be’emunato.

sources.name: Psalm 97
aliases: Still climbing through the six weekday psalms — the earth trembling, awed by something larger than itself, as the far shores go glad.
openingWords: יְיָ מָלָךְ תָּגֵל הָאָרֶץ, יִשְׂמְחוּ אִיִּים רַבִּים. עָנָן וַעֲרָפֶל סְבִיבָיו, צֶדֶק וּמִשְׁפָּט
Adonai malach, tagel ha’aretz, yism’chu iyim rabim. Anan va’arafel s’vivav, tzedek umishpat
אֵשׁ לְפָנָיו תֵּלֵךְ, וּתְלַהֵט סָבִיב צָרָיו. הֵאִירוּ בְרָקָיו תֵּבֵל, רָאֲתָה וַתָּחֵל הָאָרֶץ.
Esh l’fanav telech, ut’lahet saviv tzarav. He’iru v’rakav tevel, ra’ata vatachel ha’aretz.
שָׁמְעָה וַתִּשְׂמַח צִיּוֹן, וַתָּגֵלְנָה בְּנוֹת יְהוּדָה, לְמַעַן מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ יְיָ. כִּי־אַתָּה יְיָ עֶלְיוֹן
Sham’a vatismach Tziyon, vatagelna b’not Yehuda, l’ma’an mishpatecha Adonai. Ki ata Adonai
אֹהֲבֵי יְיָ שִׂנְאוּ־רָע, שֹׁמֵר נַפְשׁוֹת חֲסִידָיו, מִיַּד רְשָׁעִים יַצִּילֵם.
Ohavei Adonai sin’u ra, shomer nafshot chasidav, miyad r’sha’im yatzilem.

blocks.he: יְיָ מָלָךְ תָּגֵל הָאָרֶץ, יִשְׂמְחוּ אִיִּים רַבִּים. עָנָן וַעֲרָפֶל סְבִיבָיו, צֶדֶק וּמִשְׁפָּט מְכוֹן כִּסְאוֹ.
blocks.tr: Adonai malach, tagel ha’aretz, yism’chu iyim rabim. Anan va’arafel s’vivav, tzedek umishpat m’chon kis’o.

blocks.he: אֵשׁ לְפָנָיו תֵּלֵךְ, וּתְלַהֵט סָבִיב צָרָיו. הֵאִירוּ בְרָקָיו תֵּבֵל, רָאֲתָה וַתָּחֵל הָאָרֶץ. הָרִים כַּדּוֹנַג נָמַסּוּ מִלִּפְנֵי יְיָ, מִלִּפְנֵי אֲדוֹן כׇּל־הָאָרֶץ. הִגִּידוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם צִדְקוֹ, וְרָאוּ כׇל־הָעַמִּים כְּבוֹדוֹ. יֵבֹשׁוּ כׇּל־עֹבְדֵי פֶסֶל, הַמִּתְהַלְלִים בָּאֱלִילִים, הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ־לוֹ כׇּל־אֱלֹהִים.
blocks.tr: Esh l’fanav telech, ut’lahet saviv tzarav. He’iru v’rakav tevel, ra’ata vatachel ha’aretz. Harim kadonag namasu milifnei Adonai, milifnei adon kol ha’aretz. Higidu hashamayim tzidko, v’ra’u chol ha’amim k’vodo. Yevoshu kol ovdei fesel, hamit’hal’lim ba’elilim, hishtachavu lo kol elohim.

blocks.he: שָׁמְעָה וַתִּשְׂמַח צִיּוֹן, וַתָּגֵלְנָה בְּנוֹת יְהוּדָה, לְמַעַן מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ יְיָ. כִּי־אַתָּה יְיָ עֶלְיוֹן עַל־כׇּל־הָאָרֶץ, מְאֹד נַעֲלֵיתָ עַל־כׇּל־אֱלֹהִים.
blocks.tr: Sham’a vatismach Tziyon, vatagelna b’not Yehuda, l’ma’an mishpatecha Adonai. Ki ata Adonai elyon al kol ha’aretz, m’od na’aleta al kol elohim.

blocks.he: אֹהֲבֵי יְיָ שִׂנְאוּ־רָע, שֹׁמֵר נַפְשׁוֹת חֲסִידָיו, מִיַּד רְשָׁעִים יַצִּילֵם.
blocks.tr: Ohavei Adonai sin’u ra, shomer nafshot chasidav, miyad r’sha’im yatzilem.

blocks.he: אוֹר זָרֻעַ לַצַּדִּיק, וּלְיִשְׁרֵי־לֵב שִׂמְחָה. שִׂמְחוּ צַדִּיקִים בַּיְיָ, וְהוֹדוּ לְזֵכֶר קׇדְשׁוֹ.
blocks.tr: Or zaru’a latzadik, ulyishrei lev simcha. Simchu tzadikim ba’Adonai, v’hodu l’zecher kodsho.

sources.name: Psalm 98
aliases: A new song — harp, trumpets and shofar, every instrument called out by name.
openingWords: מִזְמוֹר שִׁירוּ לַיְיָ שִׁיר חָדָשׁ כִּי־נִפְלָאוֹת עָשָׂה, הוֹשִׁיעָה־לּוֹ יְמִינוֹ וּזְרוֹעַ קׇדְשׁוֹ. הוֹדִיעַ
Mizmor, shiru la’Adonai shir chadash, ki nifla’ot asah; hoshi’ah lo y’mino uzro’a
הָרִיעוּ לַיְיָ כׇּל־הָאָרֶץ, פִּצְחוּ וְרַנְּנוּ וְזַמֵּרוּ. זַמְּרוּ לַיְיָ בְּכִנּוֹר, בְּכִנּוֹר וְקוֹל זִמְרָה.
Hari’u la’Adonai kol ha’aretz, pitzchu v’ran’nu v’zameru. Zam’ru la’Adonai b’chinor, b’chinor v’kol
יִרְעַם הַיָּם וּמְלֹאוֹ, תֵּבֵל וְיֹשְׁבֵי בָהּ. נְהָרוֹת יִמְחֲאוּ־כָף, יַחַד הָרִים יְרַנֵּנוּ. לִפְנֵי־יְיָ
Yir’am hayam umlo’o, tevel v’yosh’vei vah. N’harot yimcha’u chaf, yachad harim y’ranenu.

blocks.he: מִזְמוֹר שִׁירוּ לַיְיָ שִׁיר חָדָשׁ כִּי־נִפְלָאוֹת עָשָׂה, הוֹשִׁיעָה־לּוֹ יְמִינוֹ וּזְרוֹעַ קׇדְשׁוֹ. הוֹדִיעַ יְיָ יְשׁוּעָתוֹ, לְעֵינֵי הַגּוֹיִם גִּלָּה צִדְקָתוֹ. זָכַר חַסְדּוֹ וֶאֱמוּנָתוֹ לְבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל רָאוּ כׇל־אַפְסֵי־אָרֶץ, אֵת יְשׁוּעַת אֱלֹהֵינוּ.
blocks.tr: Mizmor, shiru la’Adonai shir chadash, ki nifla’ot asah; hoshi’ah lo y’mino uzro’a kodsho. Hodi’a Adonai yeshu’ato, l’einei hagoyim gila tzidkato. Zachar chasdo ve’emunato l’veit Yisra’el, ra’u chol afsei aretz et yeshu’at Eloheinu.

blocks.he: הָרִיעוּ לַיְיָ כׇּל־הָאָרֶץ, פִּצְחוּ וְרַנְּנוּ וְזַמֵּרוּ. זַמְּרוּ לַיְיָ בְּכִנּוֹר, בְּכִנּוֹר וְקוֹל זִמְרָה. בַּחֲצֹצְרוֹת וְקוֹל שׁוֹפָר, הָרִיעוּ לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ יְיָ.
blocks.tr: Hari’u la’Adonai kol ha’aretz, pitzchu v’ran’nu v’zameru. Zam’ru la’Adonai b’chinor, b’chinor v’kol zimrah. Bachatzotz’rot v’kol shofar, hari’u lifnei haMelech Adonai.

blocks.he: יִרְעַם הַיָּם וּמְלֹאוֹ, תֵּבֵל וְיֹשְׁבֵי בָהּ. נְהָרוֹת יִמְחֲאוּ־כָף, יַחַד הָרִים יְרַנֵּנוּ. לִפְנֵי־יְיָ כִּי בָא לִשְׁפֹּט הָאָרֶץ יִשְׁפֹּט־תֵּבֵל בְּצֶדֶק, וְעַמִּים בְּמֵישָׁרִים.
blocks.tr: Yir’am hayam umlo’o, tevel v’yosh’vei vah. N’harot yimcha’u chaf, yachad harim y’ranenu. Lifnei Adonai, ki va lishpot ha’aretz; yishpot tevel b’tzedek, v’amim b’meisharim.

sources.name: Psalm 99
aliases: The last of the weekday psalms of ascent — three times it names the Holy One before we reach the storm.
openingWords: יְיָ מָלָךְ יִרְגְּזוּ עַמִּים, יֹשֵׁב כְּרוּבִים תָּנוּט הָאָרֶץ. יְיָ בְּצִיּוֹן גָּדוֹל, וְרָם
Adonai malach, yirg’zu amim; yoshev k’ruvim, tanut ha’aretz. Adonai b’Tziyon gadol, v’ram
וְעֹז מֶלֶךְ מִשְׁפָּט אָהֵב אַתָּה כּוֹנַנְתָּ מֵישָׁרִים, מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה בְּיַעֲקֹב אַתָּה עָשִׂיתָ.
V’oz melech mishpat ahev, ata konanta meisharim; mishpat utz’daka b’Ya’akov ata asita.
מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן בְּכֹהֲנָיו וּשְׁמוּאֵל בְּקֹרְאֵי שְׁמוֹ, קֹרִאים אֶל־יְיָ וְהוּא יַעֲנֵם. בְּעַמּוּד עָנָן
Moshe v’Aharon b’chohanav, ush’mu’el b’kor’ei sh’mo — kor’im el Adonai, v’hu ya’anem.
יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אַתָּה עֲנִיתָם אֵל נֹשֵׂא הָיִיתָ לָהֶם, וְנֹקֵם עַל־עֲלִילוֹתָם. רוֹמְמוּ יְיָ
Adonai Eloheinu, ata anitam; El nosei hayita lahem, v’nokem al alilotam. Rom’mu

blocks.tr: Adonai malach, yirg’zu amim; yoshev k’ruvim, tanut ha’aretz. Adonai b’Tziyon gadol, v’ram hu al kol ha’amim. Yodu shimcha gadol v’nora — kadosh hu.

blocks.he: וְעֹז מֶלֶךְ מִשְׁפָּט אָהֵב אַתָּה כּוֹנַנְתָּ מֵישָׁרִים, מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה בְּיַעֲקֹב אַתָּה עָשִׂיתָ. רוֹמְמוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְהִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַהֲדֹם רַגְלָיו קָדוֹשׁ הוּא.
blocks.tr: V’oz melech mishpat ahev, ata konanta meisharim; mishpat utz’daka b’Ya’akov ata asita. Rom’mu Adonai Eloheinu, v’hishtachavu lahadom raglav — kadosh hu.

blocks.he: מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן בְּכֹהֲנָיו וּשְׁמוּאֵל בְּקֹרְאֵי שְׁמוֹ, קֹרִאים אֶל־יְיָ וְהוּא יַעֲנֵם. בְּעַמּוּד עָנָן יְדַבֵּר אֲלֵיהֶם, שָׁמְרוּ עֵדֹתָיו וְחֹק נָתַן־לָמוֹ.
blocks.tr: Moshe v’Aharon b’chohanav, ush’mu’el b’kor’ei sh’mo — kor’im el Adonai, v’hu ya’anem. B’amud anan y’daber aleihem; shamru edotav, v’chok natan lamo.

blocks.he: יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אַתָּה עֲנִיתָם אֵל נֹשֵׂא הָיִיתָ לָהֶם, וְנֹקֵם עַל־עֲלִילוֹתָם. רוֹמְמוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְהִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְהַר קׇדְשׁוֹ, כִּי־קָדוֹשׁ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ.
blocks.tr: Adonai Eloheinu, ata anitam; El nosei hayita lahem, v’nokem al alilotam. Rom’mu Adonai Eloheinu, v’hishtachavu l’har kodsho — ki kadosh Adonai Eloheinu.

sources.name: Psalm 29
aliases: The thunderstorm psalm that crowns the week — the world’s roar resolving, in its final word, into peace.
openingWords: מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד הָבוּ לַיְיָ בְּנֵי אֵלִים, הָבוּ לַיְיָ כָּבוֹד וָעֹז. הָבוּ לַיְיָ
Mizmor l’David. Havu la’Adonai b’nei elim, havu la’Adonai kavod va’oz. Havu la’Adonai
קוֹל יְיָ עַל־הַמָּיִם אֵל־הַכָּבוֹד הִרְעִים, יְיָ עַל־מַיִם רַבִּים. קוֹל־יְיָ בַּכֹּחַ, קוֹל יְיָ
Kol Adonai al hamayim, El hakavod hir’im, Adonai al mayim rabim. Kol
קוֹל־יְיָ חֹצֵב לַהֲבוֹת אֵשׁ. קוֹל יְיָ יָחִיל מִדְבָּר, יָחִיל יְיָ מִדְבַּר קָדֵשׁ.
Kol Adonai chotzev lahavot esh. Kol Adonai yachil midbar, yachil Adonai midbar
יְיָ לַמַּבּוּל יָשָׁב, וַיֵּשֶׁב יְיָ מֶלֶךְ לְעוֹלָם. יְיָ עֹז לְעַמּוֹ יִתֵּן, יְיָ
Adonai lamabul yashav, vayeshev Adonai melech l’olam. Adonai oz l’amo yiten, Adonai

blocks.he: מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד הָבוּ לַיְיָ בְּנֵי אֵלִים, הָבוּ לַיְיָ כָּבוֹד וָעֹז. הָבוּ לַיְיָ כְּבוֹד שְׁמוֹ, הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַיְיָ בְּהַדְרַת־קֹדֶשׁ.
blocks.tr: Mizmor l’David. Havu la’Adonai b’nei elim, havu la’Adonai kavod va’oz. Havu la’Adonai k’vod sh’mo, hishtachavu la’Adonai b’hadrat kodesh.

blocks.he: קוֹל יְיָ עַל־הַמָּיִם אֵל־הַכָּבוֹד הִרְעִים, יְיָ עַל־מַיִם רַבִּים. קוֹל־יְיָ בַּכֹּחַ, קוֹל יְיָ בֶּהָדָר. קוֹל יְיָ שֹׁבֵר אֲרָזִים, וַיְשַׁבֵּר יְיָ אֶת־אַרְזֵי הַלְּבָנוֹן. וַיַּרְקִידֵם כְּמוֹ־עֵגֶל, לְבָנוֹן וְשִׂרְיֹן כְּמוֹ בֶן־רְאֵמִים.
blocks.tr: Kol Adonai al hamayim, El hakavod hir’im, Adonai al mayim rabim. Kol Adonai bako’ach, kol Adonai behadar. Kol Adonai shover arazim, vay’shaber Adonai et arzei haL’vanon. Vayarkidem k’mo egel, L’vanon v’Siryon k’mo ven r’emim.

blocks.he: קוֹל־יְיָ חֹצֵב לַהֲבוֹת אֵשׁ. קוֹל יְיָ יָחִיל מִדְבָּר, יָחִיל יְיָ מִדְבַּר קָדֵשׁ. קוֹל יְיָ יְחוֹלֵל אַיָּלוֹת וַיֶּחֱשֹׂף יְעָרוֹת וּבְהֵיכָלוֹ, כֻּלּוֹ אֹמֵר כָּבוֹד.
blocks.tr: Kol Adonai chotzev lahavot esh. Kol Adonai yachil midbar, yachil Adonai midbar Kadesh. Kol Adonai y’cholel ayalot vayechesof y’arot, uvheichalo kulo omer kavod.

blocks.he: יְיָ לַמַּבּוּל יָשָׁב, וַיֵּשֶׁב יְיָ מֶלֶךְ לְעוֹלָם. יְיָ עֹז לְעַמּוֹ יִתֵּן, יְיָ יְבָרֵךְ אֶת־עַמּוֹ בַשָּׁלוֹם.
blocks.tr: Adonai lamabul yashav, vayeshev Adonai melech l’olam. Adonai oz l’amo yiten, Adonai y’varech et amo vashalom.

sources.name: Ana B’koach
aliases: A whispered plea between the psalms and the bride — seven short lines, an ancient reaching to be set free.
openingWords: אָנָּא בְּכֹחַ גְּדֻלַּת יְמִינְךָ תַּתִּיר צְרוּרָה. קַבֵּל רִנַּת עַמְּךָ שַׂגְּבֵנוּ טַהֲרֵנוּ נוֹרָא.
Ana b’koach g’dulat y’mincha tatir tz’rura. Kabel rinat am’cha, sagvenu, taharenu, nora.
נָא גִבּוֹר דּוֹרְשֵׁי יִחוּדְךָ כְּבָבַת שָׁמְרֵם. בָּרְכֵם טַהֲרֵם רַחֲמֵם צִדְקָתְךָ תָּמִיד גָּמְלֵם.
Na gibor, dorshei yichudcha k’vavat shomrem. Barchem, taharem, rachamem, tzidkatcha tamid gomlem.
חֲסִין קָדוֹשׁ בְּרֹב טוּבְךָ נַהֵל עֲדָתֶךָ. יָחִיד גֵּאֶה לְעַמְּךָ פְּנֵה, זוֹכְרֵי קְדֻשָּׁתֶךָ.
Chasin kadosh, b’rov tuvcha nahel adatecha. Yachid ge’eh, l’am’cha p’ne, zochrei k’dushatecha.
שַׁוְעָתֵנוּ קַבֵּל וּשְׁמַע צַעֲקָתֵנוּ יוֹדֵעַ תַּעֲלוּמוֹת. בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד.
Shav’atenu kabel ushma tza’akatenu, yode’a ta’alumot. Baruch shem k’vod malchuto l’olam va’ed.

sources.name: L’cha Dodi
aliases: We rise and turn to the door: the week is behind us, and Shabbat the bride is arriving now.
openingWords: לְכָה דוֹדִי לִקְרַאת כַּלָּה, פְּנֵי שַׁבָּת נְקַבְּלָה.
L’cha dodi likrat kala, p’nei Shabbat n’kab’la.
שָׁמוֹר וְזָכוֹר בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד, הִשְׁמִיעָנוּ אֵל הַמְיוּחָד. יְיָ אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד, לְשֵׁם

blocks.tr: Shamor v’zachor b’dibur echad, hishmi’anu El ham’yuchad. Adonai echad ushmo echad, l’shem ultif’eret v’lit’hila.

blocks.he: לִקְרַאת שַׁבָּת לְכוּ וְנֵלְכָה, כִּי הִיא מְקוֹר הַבְּרָכָה. מֵרֹאשׁ מִקֶּדֶם נְסוּכָה, סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה.

blocks.he: מִקְדַּשׁ מֶלֶךְ עִיר מְלוּכָה, קוּמִי צְאִי מִתּוֹךְ הַהֲפֵכָה. רַב לָךְ שֶׁבֶת בְּעֵמֶק הַבָּכָא, וְהוּא יַחְמוֹל עָלַיִךְ חֶמְלָה.

blocks.he: הִתְנַעֲרִי מֵעָפָר קוּמִי, לִבְשִׁי בִּגְדֵי תִפְאַרְתֵּךְ עַמִּי. עַל יַד בֶּן יִשַּׁי בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי, קָרְבָה אֶל נַפְשִׁי גְאָלָהּ.
blocks.tr: Hitna’ari me’afar kumi, livshi bigdei tif’artech ami. Al yad ben Yishai beit halachmi, korva el nafshi g’ala.

blocks.he: הִתְעוֹרְרִי, הִתְעוֹרְרִי, כִּי בָא אוֹרֵךְ קוּמִי אוֹרִי. עוּרִי עוּרִי שִׁיר דַּבֵּרִי, כְּבוֹד יְיָ עָלַיִךְ נִגְלָה.
blocks.tr: Hit’or’ri, hit’or’ri, ki va orech kumi ori. Uri uri shir daberi, k’vod Adonai alayich nigla.

blocks.he: לֹא תֵבוֹשִׁי וְלֹא תִכָּלְמִי, מַה תִּשְׁתּוֹחֲחִי וּמַה תֶּהֱמִי. בָּךְ יֶחֱסוּ עֲנִיֵּי עַמִּי, וְנִבְנְתָה עִיר עַל תִּלָּהּ.
blocks.tr: Lo tevoshi v’lo tikal’mi, ma tishtochachi uma tehemi. Bach yechesu aniyei ami, v’nivn’ta ir al tila.

blocks.he: וְהָיוּ לִמְשִׁסָּה שֹׁסָיִךְ, וְרָחֲקוּ כָּל מְבַלְּעָיִךְ. יָשִׂישׂ עָלַיִךְ אֱלֹהָיִךְ, כִּמְשׂוֹשׂ חָתָן עַל כַּלָּה.
blocks.tr: V’hayu limshisa shosayich, v’rachaku kol m’val’ayich. Yasis alayich Elohayich, kimsos chatan al kala.

blocks.he: יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל תִּפְרוֹצִי, וְאֶת יְיָ תַּעֲרִיצִי. עַל יַד אִישׁ בֶּן פַּרְצִי, וְנִשְׂמְחָה וְנָגִילָה.
blocks.tr: Yamin usmol tifrotzi, v’et Adonai ta’aritzi. Al yad ish ben Partzi, v’nism’cha v’nagila.

blocks.he: בּוֹאִי בְשָׁלוֹם עֲטֶרֶת בַּעְלָהּ, גַּם בְּשִׂמְחָה וּבְצָהֳלָה. תּוֹךְ אֱמוּנֵי עַם סְגֻלָּה, בּוֹאִי כַלָּה, בּוֹאִי כַלָּה, בּוֹאִי כַלָּה שַׁבָּת מַלְכְּתָא.
blocks.tr: Bo’i v’shalom ateret ba’la, gam b’simcha uvtzohola. Toch emunei am s’gula, bo’i chala, bo’i chala, bo’i chala Shabbat malk’ta.

sources.name: Psalm 92
aliases: Shabbat has arrived — now the first psalm sung inside it, the only one the Torah names for this day.
openingWords: טוֹב לְהֹדוֹת לַיְיָ, וּלְזַמֵּר לְשִׁמְךָ עֶלְיוֹן. לְהַגִּיד בַּבֹּקֶר חַסְדֶּךָ, וֶאֱמוּנָתְךָ בַּלֵּילוֹת. עֲלֵי־עָשׂוֹר
Tov l’hodot la’Adonai, ulzamer l’shimcha elyon. L’hagid baboker chasdecha, ve’emunatcha baleilot. Alei-asor
כִּי שִׂמַּחְתַּנִי יְיָ בְּפׇעֳלֶךָ, בְּמַעֲשֵׂי יָדֶיךָ אֲרַנֵּן. מַה־גָּדְלוּ מַעֲשֶׂיךָ יְיָ, מְאֹד עָמְקוּ
Ki simachtani Adonai b’fo’olecha, b’ma’asei yadecha aranen. Mah gadlu ma’asecha Adonai, m’od
אִישׁ־בַּעַר לֹא יֵדָע, וּכְסִיל לֹא־יָבִין אֶת־זֹאת. בִּפְרֹחַ רְשָׁעִים כְּמוֹ־עֵשֶׂב וַיָּצִיצוּ כׇּל־פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן,
Ish-ba’ar lo yeda, uch’sil lo-yavin et-zot. Bifroach r’sha’im k’mo-esev, vayatzitzu kol-po’alei aven,

blocks.he: טוֹב לְהֹדוֹת לַיְיָ, וּלְזַמֵּר לְשִׁמְךָ עֶלְיוֹן. לְהַגִּיד בַּבֹּקֶר חַסְדֶּךָ, וֶאֱמוּנָתְךָ בַּלֵּילוֹת. עֲלֵי־עָשׂוֹר וַעֲלֵי־נָבֶל, עֲלֵי הִגָּיוֹן בְּכִנּוֹר.
blocks.tr: Tov l’hodot la’Adonai, ulzamer l’shimcha elyon. L’hagid baboker chasdecha, ve’emunatcha baleilot. Alei-asor va’alei-navel, alei higayon b’chinor.

blocks.he: כִּי שִׂמַּחְתַּנִי יְיָ בְּפׇעֳלֶךָ, בְּמַעֲשֵׂי יָדֶיךָ אֲרַנֵּן. מַה־גָּדְלוּ מַעֲשֶׂיךָ יְיָ, מְאֹד עָמְקוּ מַחְשְׁבֹתֶיךָ.
blocks.tr: Ki simachtani Adonai b’fo’olecha, b’ma’asei yadecha aranen. Mah gadlu ma’asecha Adonai, m’od amku machsh’votecha.

blocks.he: אִישׁ־בַּעַר לֹא יֵדָע, וּכְסִיל לֹא־יָבִין אֶת־זֹאת. בִּפְרֹחַ רְשָׁעִים כְּמוֹ־עֵשֶׂב וַיָּצִיצוּ כׇּל־פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן, לְהִשָּׁמְדָם עֲדֵי־עַד. וְאַתָּה מָרוֹם לְעֹלָם יְיָ. כִּי הִנֵּה אֹיְבֶיךָ יְיָ כִּי־הִנֵּה אֹיְבֶיךָ יֹאבֵדוּ, יִתְפָּרְדוּ כׇּל־פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן. וַתָּרֶם כִּרְאֵים קַרְנִי, בַּלֹּתִי בְּשֶׁמֶן רַעֲנָן. וַתַּבֵּט עֵינִי בְּשׁוּרָי בַּקָּמִים עָלַי מְרֵעִים תִּשְׁמַעְנָה אׇזְנָי.
blocks.tr: Ish-ba’ar lo yeda, uch’sil lo-yavin et-zot. Bifroach r’sha’im k’mo-esev, vayatzitzu kol-po’alei aven, l’hishamdam adei-ad. V’ata marom l’olam Adonai. Ki hineh oyvecha Adonai, ki-hineh oyvecha yovedu, yitpardu kol-po’alei aven. Vatarem kir’em karni, baloti b’shemen ra’anan. Vatabet eini b’shurai, bakamim alai m’re’im tishma’na oznai.

blocks.he: צַדִּיק כַּתָּמָר יִפְרָח, כְּאֶרֶז בַּלְּבָנוֹן יִשְׂגֶּה. שְׁתוּלִים בְּבֵית יְיָ, בְּחַצְרוֹת אֱלֹהֵינוּ יַפְרִיחוּ.
blocks.tr: Tzadik katamar yifrach, k’erez balvanon yisge. Sh’tulim b’veit Adonai, b’chatzrot Eloheinu yafrichu.

blocks.he: עוֹד יְנוּבוּן בְּשֵׂיבָה, דְּשֵׁנִים וְרַעֲנַנִּים יִהְיוּ. לְהַגִּיד כִּי־יָשָׁר יְיָ, צוּרִי וְלֹא־עַוְלָתָה בּוֹ.
blocks.tr: Od y’nuvun b’seiva, d’shenim v’ra’ananim yihyu. L’hagid ki-yashar Adonai, tzuri v’lo-avlata bo.

sources.name: Psalm 93
aliases: The psalm of Friday itself — we close the week by singing the very crown creation sang when it was new.
openingWords: יְיָ מָלָךְ גֵּאוּת לָבֵשׁ לָבֵשׁ יְיָ עֹז הִתְאַזָּר, אַף־תִּכּוֹן תֵּבֵל בַּל־תִּמּוֹט.
Adonai malach geut lavesh, lavesh Adonai oz hit’azar, af-tikon tevel bal-timot.
נָכוֹן כִּסְאֲךָ מֵאָז, מֵעוֹלָם אָתָּה. נָשְׂאוּ נְהָרוֹת יְיָ נָשְׂאוּ נְהָרוֹת קוֹלָם, יִשְׂאוּ
Nachon kis’acha me’az, me’olam ata. Nasu n’harot Adonai, nasu n’harot kolam, yisu
מִקֹּלוֹת מַיִם רַבִּים אַדִּירִים מִשְׁבְּרֵי־יָם, אַדִּיר בַּמָּרוֹם יְיָ.
Mikolot mayim rabim, adirim mishb’rei-yam, adir bamarom Adonai.
עֵדֹתֶיךָ נֶאֶמְנוּ מְאֹד לְבֵיתְךָ נַאֲוָה־קֹדֶשׁ, יְיָ לְאֹרֶךְ יָמִים.
Edotecha ne’emnu m’od, l’veitcha naava-kodesh, Adonai l’orech yamim.

blocks.he: יְיָ מָלָךְ גֵּאוּת לָבֵשׁ לָבֵשׁ יְיָ עֹז הִתְאַזָּר, אַף־תִּכּוֹן תֵּבֵל בַּל־תִּמּוֹט.
blocks.tr: Adonai malach geut lavesh, lavesh Adonai oz hit’azar, af-tikon tevel bal-timot.

blocks.he: נָכוֹן כִּסְאֲךָ מֵאָז, מֵעוֹלָם אָתָּה. נָשְׂאוּ נְהָרוֹת יְיָ נָשְׂאוּ נְהָרוֹת קוֹלָם, יִשְׂאוּ נְהָרוֹת דׇּכְיָם.
blocks.tr: Nachon kis’acha me’az, me’olam ata. Nasu n’harot Adonai, nasu n’harot kolam, yisu n’harot dochyam.

blocks.he: מִקֹּלוֹת מַיִם רַבִּים אַדִּירִים מִשְׁבְּרֵי־יָם, אַדִּיר בַּמָּרוֹם יְיָ.
blocks.tr: Mikolot mayim rabim, adirim mishb’rei-yam, adir bamarom Adonai.

blocks.he: עֵדֹתֶיךָ נֶאֶמְנוּ מְאֹד לְבֵיתְךָ נַאֲוָה־קֹדֶשׁ, יְיָ לְאֹרֶךְ יָמִים.
blocks.tr: Edotecha ne’emnu m’od, l’veitcha naava-kodesh, Adonai l’orech yamim.

sources.name: Bar’chu
aliases: The formal call to prayer — a room of individuals becomes a community, everyone facing the same center.

sources.name: Ma’ariv Aravim
aliases: Night falls, and the blessing turns cosmic — we are stardust on a small blue speck, one piece of an enormous story.
openingWords: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר בִּדְבָרוֹ מַעֲרִיב עֲרָבִים בְּחָכְמָה פּוֹתֵחַ
Baruch ata Adonai, Eloheinu melech ha’olam, asher bidvaro ma’ariv aravim, b’chochma poteach
בּוֹרֵא יוֹם וָלָיְלָה גּוֹלֵל אוֹר מִפְּנֵי חֹשֶׁךְ וְחֹשֶׁךְ מִפְּנֵי אוֹר וּמַעֲבִיר יוֹם
Borei yom valayla, golel or mipnei choshech v’choshech mipnei or, uma’avir yom
אֵל חַי וְקַיָּם תָּמִיד יִמְלֹךְ עָלֵינוּ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַמַּעֲרִיב
El chai v’kayam tamid yimloch aleinu l’olam va’ed. Baruch ata Adonai, hama’ariv

blocks.he: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר בִּדְבָרוֹ מַעֲרִיב עֲרָבִים בְּחָכְמָה פּוֹתֵחַ שְׁעָרִים וּבִתְבוּנָה מְשַׁנֶּה עִתִּים וּמַחֲלִיף אֶת־הַזְּמַנִּים וּמְסַדֵּר אֶת־הַכּוֹכָבִים בְּמִשְׁמְרוֹתֵיהֶם בָּרָקִיעַ כִּרְצוֹנוֹ.
blocks.tr: Baruch ata Adonai, Eloheinu melech ha’olam, asher bidvaro ma’ariv aravim, b’chochma poteach sh’arim, uvitvuna m’shaneh itim umachalif et haz’manim, umsader et hakochavim b’mishm’roteihem baraki’a kirtzono.

blocks.he: בּוֹרֵא יוֹם וָלָיְלָה גּוֹלֵל אוֹר מִפְּנֵי חֹשֶׁךְ וְחֹשֶׁךְ מִפְּנֵי אוֹר וּמַעֲבִיר יוֹם וּמֵבִיא לָיְלָה וּמַבְדִּיל בֵּין יוֹם וּבֵין לָיְלָה יְיָ צְבָאוֹת שְׁמוֹ.
blocks.tr: Borei yom valayla, golel or mipnei choshech v’choshech mipnei or, uma’avir yom umevi layla, umavdil bein yom uvein layla, Adonai tz’va’ot sh’mo.

blocks.he: אֵל חַי וְקַיָּם תָּמִיד יִמְלֹךְ עָלֵינוּ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַמַּעֲרִיב עֲרָבִים.
blocks.tr: El chai v’kayam tamid yimloch aleinu l’olam va’ed. Baruch ata Adonai, hama’ariv aravim.

sources.name: Ahavat Olam
aliases: Love as mutual obligation — to those who came before us, those beside us, and most of all those still to come.
openingWords: אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמְּךָ אָהָבְתָּ תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת חֻקִּים וּמִשְׁפָּטִים אוֹתָנוּ לִמַּדְתָּ.
Ahavat olam beit Yisra’el am’cha ahavta, Tora umitzvot, chukim umishpatim otanu limadta.
עַל כֵּן יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּשָׁכְבֵנוּ וּבְקוּמֵנוּ נָשִׂיחַ בְּחֻקֶּיךָ וְנִשְׂמַח בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָתֶךָ וּבְמִצְוֹתֶיךָ
Al ken Adonai Eloheinu b’shochveinu uvkumeinu nasi’ach b’chukecha, v’nismach b’divrei Toratecha uvmitzvotecha
כִּי הֵם חַיֵּינוּ וְאֹרֶךְ יָמֵינוּ וּבָהֶם נֶהְגֶּה יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה. וְאַהֲבָתְךָ אַל תָּסִיר
Ki hem chayeinu v’orech yameinu, uvahem neh’ge yomam valayla. V’ahavatcha al tasir

blocks.he: אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמְּךָ אָהָבְתָּ תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת חֻקִּים וּמִשְׁפָּטִים אוֹתָנוּ לִמַּדְתָּ.
blocks.tr: Ahavat olam beit Yisra’el am’cha ahavta, Tora umitzvot, chukim umishpatim otanu limadta.

blocks.he: עַל כֵּן יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּשָׁכְבֵנוּ וּבְקוּמֵנוּ נָשִׂיחַ בְּחֻקֶּיךָ וְנִשְׂמַח בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָתֶךָ וּבְמִצְוֹתֶיךָ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד.
blocks.tr: Al ken Adonai Eloheinu b’shochveinu uvkumeinu nasi’ach b’chukecha, v’nismach b’divrei Toratecha uvmitzvotecha l’olam va’ed.

blocks.he: כִּי הֵם חַיֵּינוּ וְאֹרֶךְ יָמֵינוּ וּבָהֶם נֶהְגֶּה יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה. וְאַהֲבָתְךָ אַל תָּסִיר מִמֶּנּוּ לְעוֹלָמִים. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אוֹהֵב עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
blocks.tr: Ki hem chayeinu v’orech yameinu, uvahem neh’ge yomam valayla. V’ahavatcha al tasir mimenu l’olamim. Baruch ata Adonai, ohev amo Yisra’el.

sources.name: The Sh’ma
aliases: The line we say lying down and rising up, and hope to say last of all — Israel’s whole faith in six words.
openingWords: שְׁמַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יְיָ֥ אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יְיָ֥ ׀ אֶחָֽד׃
Sh’ma Yisra’el, Adonai Eloheinu, Adonai echad.

blocks.he: שְׁמַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יְיָ֥ אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יְיָ֥ ׀ אֶחָֽד׃
blocks.tr: Sh’ma Yisra’el, Adonai Eloheinu, Adonai echad.

sources.name: V’ahavta & Tzitzit
aliases: And now the answer: love with all your heart — bound to the hand, worn on the fringe, spoken to the children.
openingWords: וְאָ֣הַבְתָּ֔ אֵ֖ת יְיָ֣ אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ בְּכׇל־לְבָבְךָ֥ וּבְכׇל־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ וּבְכׇל־מְאֹדֶֽךָ׃ וְהָי֞וּ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֧י
V’ahavta et Adonai Elohecha, b’chol l’vavcha uvchol nafsh’cha uvchol m’odecha. V’hayu had’varim
וּקְשַׁרְתָּ֥ם לְא֖וֹת עַל־יָדֶ֑ךָ וְהָי֥וּ לְטֹטָפֹ֖ת בֵּ֥ין עֵינֶֽיךָ׃ וּכְתַבְתָּ֛ם עַל־מְזֻז֥וֹת בֵּיתֶ֖ךָ וּבִשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ׃
Uk’shartam l’ot al yadecha, v’hayu l’totafot bein einecha. Uch’tavtam al m’zuzot beitecha
וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־שָׁמֹ֤עַ תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל־מִצְוֺתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם לְאַהֲבָ֞ה אֶת־יְיָ֤ אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙
V’haya im shamoa tishm’u el mitzvotai asher anochi m’tzaveh etchem hayom, l’ahava
הִשָּֽׁמְר֣וּ לָכֶ֔ם פֶּ֥ן יִפְתֶּ֖ה לְבַבְכֶ֑ם וְסַרְתֶּ֗ם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם לָהֶֽם׃ וְחָרָ֨ה
Hisham’ru lachem pen yifteh l’vavchem, v’sartem va’avadtem elohim acherim v’hishtachavitem lahem. V’chara

blocks.he: וְאָ֣הַבְתָּ֔ אֵ֖ת יְיָ֣ אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ בְּכׇל־לְבָבְךָ֥ וּבְכׇל־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ וּבְכׇל־מְאֹדֶֽךָ׃ וְהָי֞וּ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֧י מְצַוְּךָ֛ הַיּ֖וֹם עַל־לְבָבֶֽךָ׃ וְשִׁנַּנְתָּ֣ם לְבָנֶ֔יךָ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֖ בָּ֑ם בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ֤ בְּבֵיתֶ֙ךָ֙ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ֣ בַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וּֽבְשׇׁכְבְּךָ֖ וּבְקוּמֶֽךָ׃
blocks.tr: V’ahavta et Adonai Elohecha, b’chol l’vavcha uvchol nafsh’cha uvchol m’odecha. V’hayu had’varim ha’eleh asher anochi m’tzav’cha hayom al l’vavecha. V’shinantam l’vanecha v’dibarta bam, b’shivt’cha b’veitecha uvlecht’cha vaderech, uvshochb’cha uvkumecha.

blocks.he: וּקְשַׁרְתָּ֥ם לְא֖וֹת עַל־יָדֶ֑ךָ וְהָי֥וּ לְטֹטָפֹ֖ת בֵּ֥ין עֵינֶֽיךָ׃ וּכְתַבְתָּ֛ם עַל־מְזֻז֥וֹת בֵּיתֶ֖ךָ וּבִשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ׃
blocks.tr: Uk’shartam l’ot al yadecha, v’hayu l’totafot bein einecha. Uch’tavtam al m’zuzot beitecha uvish’arecha.

blocks.he: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־שָׁמֹ֤עַ תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל־מִצְוֺתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם לְאַהֲבָ֞ה אֶת־יְיָ֤ אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ וּלְעׇבְד֔וֹ בְּכׇל־לְבַבְכֶ֖ם וּבְכׇל־נַפְשְׁכֶֽם׃ וְנָתַתִּ֧י מְטַֽר־אַרְצְכֶ֛ם בְּעִתּ֖וֹ יוֹרֶ֣ה וּמַלְק֑וֹשׁ וְאָסַפְתָּ֣ דְגָנֶ֔ךָ וְתִירֹֽשְׁךָ֖ וְיִצְהָרֶֽךָ׃ וְנָתַתִּ֛י עֵ֥שֶׂב בְּשָׂדְךָ֖ לִבְהֶמְתֶּ֑ךָ וְאָכַלְתָּ֖ וְשָׂבָֽעְתָּ׃
blocks.tr: V’haya im shamoa tishm’u el mitzvotai asher anochi m’tzaveh etchem hayom, l’ahava et Adonai Eloheichem ul’ovdo b’chol l’vavchem uvchol nafsh’chem. V’natati m’tar artz’chem b’ito, yoreh umalkosh, v’asafta d’ganecha v’tirosh’cha v’yitzharecha. V’natati esev b’sad’cha liv’hemtecha, v’achalta v’sava’ta.

blocks.he: הִשָּֽׁמְר֣וּ לָכֶ֔ם פֶּ֥ן יִפְתֶּ֖ה לְבַבְכֶ֑ם וְסַרְתֶּ֗ם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם לָהֶֽם׃ וְחָרָ֨ה אַף־יְיָ֜ בָּכֶ֗ם וְעָצַ֤ר אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה מָטָ֔ר וְהָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה לֹ֥א תִתֵּ֖ן אֶת־יְבוּלָ֑הּ וַאֲבַדְתֶּ֣ם מְהֵרָ֗ה מֵעַל֙ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַטֹּבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְיָ֖ נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶֽם׃
blocks.tr: Hisham’ru lachem pen yifteh l’vavchem, v’sartem va’avadtem elohim acherim v’hishtachavitem lahem. V’chara af Adonai bachem, v’atzar et hashamayim v’lo yihyeh matar, v’ha’adama lo titen et y’vulah, va’avadtem m’hera me’al ha’aretz hatova asher Adonai noten lachem.

blocks.he: וְשַׂמְתֶּם֙ אֶת־דְּבָרַ֣י אֵ֔לֶּה עַל־לְבַבְכֶ֖ם וְעַֽל־נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם וּקְשַׁרְתֶּ֨ם אֹתָ֤ם לְאוֹת֙ עַל־יֶדְכֶ֔ם וְהָי֥וּ לְטוֹטָפֹ֖ת בֵּ֥ין עֵינֵיכֶֽם׃ וְלִמַּדְתֶּ֥ם אֹתָ֛ם אֶת־בְּנֵיכֶ֖ם לְדַבֵּ֣ר בָּ֑ם בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ֤ בְּבֵיתֶ֙ךָ֙ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ֣ בַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וּֽבְשׇׁכְבְּךָ֖ וּבְקוּמֶֽךָ׃ וּכְתַבְתָּ֛ם עַל־מְזוּז֥וֹת בֵּיתֶ֖ךָ וּבִשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ׃ לְמַ֨עַן יִרְבּ֤וּ יְמֵיכֶם֙ וִימֵ֣י בְנֵיכֶ֔ם עַ֚ל הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְיָ֛ לַאֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם לָתֵ֣ת לָהֶ֑ם כִּימֵ֥י הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
blocks.tr: V’samtem et d’varai eleh al l’vavchem v’al nafsh’chem, uk’shartem otam l’ot al yedchem, v’hayu l’totafot bein eineichem. V’limadtem otam et b’neichem l’daber bam, b’shivt’cha b’veitecha uvlecht’cha vaderech, uvshochb’cha uvkumecha. Uch’tavtam al m’zuzot beitecha uvish’arecha. L’ma’an yirbu y’meichem vimei v’neichem al ha’adama asher nishba Adonai la’avoteichem latet lahem, kimei hashamayim al ha’aretz.

blocks.he: דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וְעָשׂ֨וּ לָהֶ֥ם צִיצִ֛ת עַל־כַּנְפֵ֥י בִגְדֵיהֶ֖ם לְדֹרֹתָ֑ם וְנָ֥תְנ֛וּ עַל־צִיצִ֥ת הַכָּנָ֖ף פְּתִ֥יל תְּכֵֽלֶת׃
blocks.tr: Daber el b’nei Yisra’el v’amarta alehem, v’asu lahem tzitzit al kanfei vig’deihem l’dorotam, v’natnu al tzitzit hakanaf p’til t’chelet.

blocks.he: וְהָיָ֣ה לָכֶם֮ לְצִיצִת֒ וּרְאִיתֶ֣ם אֹת֗וֹ וּזְכַרְתֶּם֙ אֶת־כׇּל־מִצְוֺ֣ת יְיָ֔ וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־תָת֜וּרוּ אַחֲרֵ֤י לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְאַחֲרֵ֣י עֵֽינֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֥ם זֹנִ֖ים אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃
blocks.tr: V’haya lachem l’tzitzit, ur’item oto uz’chartem et kol mitzvot Adonai, va’asitem otam, v’lo taturu acharei l’vavchem v’acharei eineichem asher atem zonim achareihem.

blocks.he: לְמַ֣עַן תִּזְכְּר֔וּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֶת־כׇּל־מִצְוֺתָ֑י וִהְיִיתֶ֥ם קְדֹשִׁ֖ים לֵאלֹֽהֵיכֶֽם׃ אֲנִ֞י יְיָ֣ אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצֵ֤אתִי אֶתְכֶם֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לִהְי֥וֹת לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִ֑ים אֲנִ֖י יְיָ֥ אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
blocks.tr: L’ma’an tizk’ru va’asitem et kol mitzvotai, vih’yitem k’doshim leloheichem. Ani Adonai Eloheichem, asher hotzeti etchem me’eretz Mitzrayim lihyot lachem lelohim, ani Adonai Eloheichem.

sources.name: Emet v’Emunah
aliases: The blessing turns from declaring the One to begging for freedom — belief voiced from a place of powerlessness.
openingWords: אֱמֶת וֶאֱמוּנָה כָּל־זֹאת וְקַיָּם עָלֵינוּ כִּי הוּא יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְאֵין זוּלָתוֹ וַאֲנַחְנוּ
Emet ve’emuna kol zot v’kayam aleinu, ki hu Adonai Eloheinu v’ein zulato,
הַשָּׂם נַפְשֵׁנוּ בַּחַיִּים וְלֹא־נָתַן לַמּוֹט רַגְלֵנוּ.
Hasam nafsheinu bachayim, v’lo natan lamot ragleinu.
הָעֹשֶׂה לָּנוּ נִסִּים וַיּוֹצֵא אֶת־עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִתּוֹכָם לְחֵרוּת עוֹלָם.
Ha’oseh lanu nisim, vayotze et amo Yisra’el mitocham l’cherut olam.
הַמַּעֲבִיר בָּנָיו בֵּין גִּזְרֵי יַם סוּף. וְרָאוּ בָנָיו גְּבוּרָתוֹ שִׁבְּחוּ וְהוֹדוּ לִשְׁמוֹ.
Hama’avir banav bein gizrei yam suf. V’ra’u vanav g’vurato, shib’chu v’hodu lishmo.

blocks.he: אֱמֶת וֶאֱמוּנָה כָּל־זֹאת וְקַיָּם עָלֵינוּ כִּי הוּא יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְאֵין זוּלָתוֹ וַאֲנַחְנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמּוֹ. הַפּוֹדֵנוּ מִיַּד מְלָכִים מַלְכֵּנוּ הַגּוֹאֲלֵנוּ מִכַּף כָּל־הֶעָרִיצִים.
blocks.tr: Emet ve’emuna kol zot v’kayam aleinu, ki hu Adonai Eloheinu v’ein zulato, va’anachnu Yisra’el amo. Hapodeinu miyad m’lachim malkeinu, hago’aleinu mikaf kol he’aritzim.

sources.name: Mi Chamocha
aliases: The song at the shore, sung again tonight — the moment slavery broke open and a people first sang free.
openingWords: מִֽי־כָמֹ֤כָה בָּֽאֵלִם֙ יְיָ֔ מִ֥י כָּמֹ֖כָה נֶאְדָּ֣ר בַּקֹּ֑דֶשׁ נוֹרָ֥א תְהִלֹּ֖ת עֹ֥שֵׂה פֶֽלֶא׃
Mi chamocha ba’elim Adonai, mi kamocha nedar bakodesh, nora t’hilot oseh fele.
מַלְכוּתְךָ רָאוּ בָנֶיךָ, בּוֹקֵעַ יָם לִפְנֵי מֹשֶׁה וּמִרְיָם, זֶה אֵלִי עָנוּ וְאָמְרוּ:
Malchut’cha ra’u vanecha, bokea yam lifnei Moshe uMiryam, zeh Eli anu v’amru:
וְנֶאֱמַר כִּי־פָדָה יְיָ אֶת יַעֲקֹב וּגְאָלוֹ מִיַּד חָזָק מִמֶּנּוּ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ
